name: Nmap
purpose: Targeted TCP/UDP host and service discovery
inputs: explicit scoped hosts, protocol, bounded ports
expected_output: host state, port state, service probe evidence
interpretation: open is reachable service candidate; filtered/unknown is not closed; banner is not patch proof
limitations: vantage/firewall/protocol/rate affect coverage; UDP silence ambiguous
alternatives: RustScan for candidate discovery then Nmap confirmation
Netcat for one known protocol endpoint

name: RustScan
purpose: Fast bounded TCP port candidate discovery
requirements: Installed binary and carefully bounded rate/ports
use_cases: approved lab or explicitly allowed network discovery
interpretation: confirm candidates with protocol-aware probes; silence is inconclusive
limitations: higher traffic profile; firewall and rate controls may distort results
mode: active; explicit scope and rate required

name: curl
interpretation: compare controlled requests; response alone may be cache/proxy/application behavior
limitations: does not emulate browser execution or full client state

name: Burp Suite
purpose: Intercept, inspect, and manually replay web traffic
requirements: Installed application; browser proxy setup; licensed features may vary
inputs: browser traffic and explicit target scope
example: Configure a local browser proxy, capture one in-scope request, compare controlled variants
interpretation: manual evidence needs controlled identities and expected-boundary comparison
limitations: GUI workflows not available in headless hosts; automation features vary

name: OWASP ZAP
purpose: Web proxy and optional automated web testing
requirements: Installed; automation add-ons/configuration may be required
use_cases: proxy inspection and approved bounded application checks
example: Use manual proxy mode for a single scoped request; use automation only with reviewed policy
interpretation: alerts are hypotheses requiring manual reproduction
limitations: scanner can create state/load; coverage and rules vary
mode: manual proxy or active scanner; scanner requires explicit permission

name: ffuf
use_cases: authorized challenge or expressly permitted scoped route discovery
inputs: one in-scope base, small wordlist, rate/depth limits
example: Use only an approved bounded wordlist with a measured not-found baseline
interpretation: compare baseline responses; candidates are not vulnerabilities
limitations: traffic volume, custom errors, and shared hosting cause noise

name: Nuclei
purpose: Template-based detection of known exposure patterns
requirements: Installed binary, current reviewed templates, explicit allowlist
use_cases: narrow authorized checks after applicability review
example: Review selected template requests and impact before a scoped run
interpretation: match is not confirmation; reproduce manually and verify applicability
limitations: templates can be intrusive/stale and produce false positives
mode: active; explicit template review and permission required

name: dig
purpose: Query DNS records and resolver responses
requirements: dig or nslookup available; approved names
interpretation: record presence is time/resolver-specific; no result does not prove no asset
limitations: does not establish ownership or authorization

name: Wireshark/TShark
purpose: Capture or analyze packet traces and protocol flows
requirements: TShark/Wireshark installed; capture permissions for live capture
use_cases: challenge PCAP analysis and approved troubleshooting
inputs: existing capture or explicitly authorized interface/filter
interpretation: summaries guide focused stream inspection; encrypted payload remains opaque without authorized keys
limitations: capture may contain credentials/personal data; live capture privilege varies
mode: offline analysis preferred; live capture needs permission

name: file/readelf/objdump/strings
purpose: Identify and inspect executable format, headers, symbols, disassembly, and strings
use_cases: initial ELF/PE triage and static analysis
expected_output: format, architecture, sections, symbols and printable strings
interpretation: strings/imports are clues; correlate with code/control flow

name: Ghidra
purpose: Disassembly, decompilation, cross-reference and PE/ELF analysis
requirements: Installed release and compatible Java runtime; GUI or analyzeHeadless
use_cases: static reverse engineering and function/control-flow analysis
example: Import a local sample, select detected architecture, inspect entry point/import xrefs
interpretation: decompiler is an approximation; verify important behavior in assembly/dynamic trace
limitations: packed/obfuscated code and incorrect types can mislead; GUI unavailable headless
mode: offline analysis; execute samples only isolated

name: GDB/pwndbg
purpose: Debug Linux binaries and inspect process state
use_cases: controlled local challenge crash and behavior analysis
inputs: local challenge binary and reproducible test input
example: Run a local challenge binary under GDB and inspect the faulting instruction
interpretation: crash location is evidence about failure, not automatically control-flow control

name: BloodHound/SharpHound
purpose: Collect and visualize authorized AD relationship data
operating_systems: BloodHound server: Linux/Windows; SharpHound collector: Windows
requirements: Approved domain identity, collector compatibility, storage controls, collection authorization
use_cases: relationship/path analysis in scoped AD reviews
example: Review collection options and scope before importing a bounded dataset
interpretation: edges reflect collected state and need source ACL/policy validation
limitations: collection is noisy/sensitive and may be incomplete/stale

name: ldapsearch/NetExec/Impacket
purpose: Directory/protocol enumeration utilities for authorized AD work
requirements: Installed exact versions, approved identity, target and query scope
use_cases: LDAP metadata, SMB protocol facts, Kerberos/network protocol tasks
inputs: explicit DC/domain, identity and bounded query
example: Use a least-privilege LDAP query for a defined base and small attribute set
interpretation: access denied/partial results show visibility limits, not absence; auth actions need separate approval
limitations: tool flags/version differ; broad collection can expose sensitive data
mode: read-only only where configured; authentication/action-specific approval required

name: PowerShell/Windows built-ins
purpose: Read-only local Windows inventory and policy review
requirements: Authorized local session; PowerShell availability and policy constraints
use_cases: identity, services, tasks, network, installed software and event review
interpretation: output visibility depends on token/policy; presence alone is not weakness
limitations: language mode/permissions/version affect commands and output

name: Linux built-ins
purpose: Read-only host, identity, process, socket, permission and service inventory
requirements: Authorized local shell; command availability varies
expected_output: identity, kernel and listening socket facts
interpretation: permissions and missing commands constrain visibility
limitations: container, namespace, procfs, and privilege limitations
